<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915410_theRebbe_669" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915410_theRebbe_669__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,</t>
    <t s="2">Yud Kislev 5746*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" was recited by Dovid and by several Rebbes on their respective redemption days.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me."</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known,</t>
    <t s="2">that in addition to the simple meaning of the matter, that this verse was said by Dovid regarding his own redemption,</t>
    <t s="3">that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed him from the wars that came upon him,</t>
    <t s="4">this verse also alludes to the redemption of several tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="5">and certainly the redemption of the tzaddikim who said this verse at the time they were redeemed.</t>
    <t s="6">And it is noteworthy,</t>
    <t s="7">that in all three redemptions of our Nesi'im — the redemption of the Alter Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev,</t>
    <t s="8">the redemption of the Mitteler Rebbe on Yud Kislev,</t>
    <t s="9">and the redemption of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, on Yud-Beis Tammuz — the masters of the redemption said this verse on the day they were redeemed.</t>
    <t s="10">Regarding the redemption of the Alter Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev, it is known what the Alter Rebbe wrote in his holy letter,</t>
    <t s="11">"When I read in the book of Tehillim the verse 'He redeemed my soul in peace,' etc., I went out in peace, from Hashem is peace."</t>
    <t s="12">Regarding the redemption of the Mitteler Rebbe on Yud Kislev,</t>
    <t s="13">it is known</t>
    <t s="14">that our Nesi'im would recite the daily portion of Tehillim as divided by the days of the month,</t>
    <t s="15">and since the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is in the monthly Tehillim portion for the tenth day of the month,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore, on the day of his redemption</t>
    <t s="17">(the tenth of Kislev)</t>
    <t s="18">he said this verse.</t>
    <t s="19">And regarding the redemption of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, on Yud-Beis Tammuz,</t>
    <t s="20">it is known</t>
    <t s="21">the custom of our Nesi'im that in special times and situations they would add the recitation of the Tehillim portion as divided by the days of the week</t>
    <t s="22">(in addition to the monthly Tehillim portion),</t>
    <t s="23">and since the date of Yud-Beis Tammuz in the year 5687</t>
    <t s="24">(the year of the arrest and redemption)</t>
    <t s="25">fell on the third day of the week, and the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is in the weekly Tehillim portion for the third day of the week,</t>
    <t s="26">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="27">that the master of the redemption of Yud-Beis Tammuz said this verse on the day of his redemption.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the connection of the Yud Kislev redemption to this verse is even more pronounced than the others, as it recurs annually.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="1">that the connection of the redemption of Yud Kislev to the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is</t>
    <t s="2">(in one aspect)</t>
    <t s="3">even greater than the connection of the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz to this verse,</t>
    <t s="4">for since this verse is in the Tehillim portion for the tenth day of the month,</t>
    <t s="5">the connection of this verse to</t>
    <t s="6">[the redemption of]</t>
    <t s="7">Yud Kislev is emphasized every single year.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
